definition: Google OR-Tools is a free and open-source software suite developed by Google for solving linear programming (LP), mixed integer programming (MIP), constraint programming (CP), vehicle routing (VRP), and related optimization problems.
details: OR stands for operations research. OR-Tools is a set of components written in C++ but provides wrappers for Java, .NET and Python. It is distributed under the Apache License 2.0.

explainer.lead: It is a free, open-source Google software suite for optimisation problems including linear and mixed integer programming, constraint programming and vehicle routing. It matters because it packages several solver families in one library with multiple language bindings.

tiers.eli5: It's a toolbox for solving scheduling and routing puzzles as well as possible.
tiers.practitioner: Written in C++ with wrappers for Java, .NET and Python, it is used to model LP, MIP, CP and VRP problems; the right solver choice depends on the problem structure.
tiers.paperLevel: A suite for linear programming, mixed integer programming, constraint programming and vehicle routing; OR stands for operations research. No single solver is specified as universally best.

explainer.example: A delivery company models a vehicle routing problem with OR-Tools to assign stops to vehicles.
